rule: Each subject must have a unique subject identifier.
Age must be present and within 18-100 years (assumed plausibility limits, not a clinical rule).
Sex must be one of M, F, U.
Reference start date must not be after reference end date.
Every date that is present must be a valid ISO 8601 date (complete or partial) and a real calendar date.
Every adverse event must belong to a subject who exists in Demographics.
AE end date must not be before AE start date.
The reported adverse event term must be present.
Every reported AE term must have a coded dictionary term (AE not coded).
Serious event flag must be Y or N.
A serious adverse event must have an outcome recorded.
AE start date before the subject's reference start date (pre-treatment event). Flag for review.
The same adverse event must not be recorded twice.
Systolic blood pressure must be within 60-250 mmHg (assumed plausibility limits, not a clinical rule).
Diastolic blood pressure must not be higher than systolic blood pressure from the same measurement.
Pulse must be within 30-200 beats/min and temperature within 34-42 °C (assumed plausibility limits, not clinical rules).
A vital sign result that is present must have a unit.
A result outside the normal range must be flagged as abnormal in LBNRIND.
A laboratory result that is present must have a standard unit, for tests that are reported with a unit.
Visit dates must be in chronological order of VISITNUM within each subject.
